outcomes.text: From one request to the Dispatcher, devbench creates a central multi-repo work folder with git worktrees, launches persistent Owner and optional domain-worker sessions in Herdr, tracks Herdr and AI session IDs/states for resumption, and archives the entire work folder cleanly when done.

ucs.title: Configure devbench from template
ucs.summary: The user installs devbench from its marketplace repo and initializes an external-first user config (~/.devbench/config.json, or $DEVBENCH_CONFIG) from the committed template with their work root, archive root, repo aliases, and default agent CLI commands.

flows.title: External user config initialized and validated

touchpoints.sees: Validation summary confirming config path, work root, repo aliases, and default agent commands

flows.title: Malformed JSON or missing required field

touchpoints.sees: Exact JSON line/column or missing required field name with no partial overwrite

flows.title: Configured repo path missing or not a Git repo

touchpoints.sees: List of offending repo aliases and paths to fix before running devbench new

flows.title: DEVBENCH_CONFIG environment variable set

touchpoints.sees: Init and validation target the custom DEVBENCH_CONFIG path instead of ~/.devbench/config.json

flows.title: User config file already exists

touchpoints.sees: Existing config left untouched; template diff lists any newly added keys only

ucs.title: Setup workspace
ucs.summary: The user starts a named work targeting one or more repos; devbench preflights every repo, creates a central workspace folder under the configured work root, auto-provisions a git worktree and task branch per repo inside it, and writes initial work state centrally.

flows.title: Workspace folder, repo worktrees, and central state created

touchpoints.sees: Central work folder path, task branch names, worktree paths, and active state record

flows.title: Preflight fails (unknown alias, branch exists, or folder collision)

touchpoints.sees: Exact failing repo/branch/folder reason; zero folders or worktrees created

flows.title: Second repo worktree fails mid-setup

touchpoints.sees: Repo 1 worktree rolled back cleanly, state marked failed, error reported

flows.title: Windows reserved name, case collision, or long path

touchpoints.sees: Sanitized slug suggestion or early stop before hitting Windows 260-char or reserved-name errors

flows.title: Source repo has local uncommitted changes or duplicate alias

touchpoints.sees: Aliases deduplicated, clean worktree branched from base_ref, base_sha recorded in state

ucs.title: Launch Owner or domain-worker session and save AI session ID
ucs.summary: The Dispatcher (or Owner) opens or reuses the work's dedicated 1:1 Herdr workspace via herdr-app, launches an Owner (primary pane) or domain-worker session (tab or side pane) via herdr-core with --outlive-parent and herdr.space=<id>, verifies first_message.sent, and saves all three session IDs plus cwd centrally.

flows.title: Owner or domain-worker session launched and state recorded

touchpoints.sees: Confirmation with role/domain, 1:1 Herdr workspace and pane target, hc terminal ID, and saved AI session ID

flows.title: Agent paused on trust dialog (first_message.sent=false)

touchpoints.sees: Session marked blocked with hc read screen preview; no blind resend or --force bypass

flows.title: Herdr app or core not running, or launch fails after space.new

touchpoints.sees: Orphan space cleaned up if created, state marked failed, clear prompt to open Herdr first

flows.title: Target role terminal db-<slug>-<role> is already live

touchpoints.sees: Existing live terminal focused/reused idempotently without spawning a duplicate agent

flows.title: Native AI session ID unavailable at launch (e.g. agy or delayed rollout)

touchpoints.sees: Launch succeeds with capture=pending|manual; Dispatcher can bind or supply ID later on resume

ucs.title: Inspect and resume work or AI session
ucs.summary: The user checks all works from the central state directory reconciled against live Herdr, sends follow-up prompts, or resumes a paused or disconnected session by rechecking its saved native AI session ID (or accepting an explicit ID) in its recorded cwd.

flows.title: Central work status reconciled and session resumed

touchpoints.sees: Reconciled work/session status table and focused or resumed agent pane

flows.title: hc terminal gone after reboot (not_found or finished)

touchpoints.sees: Space recreated if missing; harness relaunched with resume argv and saved or passed session ID in recorded cwd

flows.title: Session blocked on permission prompt or worktree missing

touchpoints.sees: Human-attention warning showing screen snippet or missing worktree path; never forces past prompt

flows.title: hc terminal is still live (even if hidden)

touchpoints.sees: Existing terminal reattached and focused via herdr-app without creating a duplicate session

flows.title: State opened on another device without local AI history

touchpoints.sees: Graceful fallback notice: recreates worktrees from git branches and starts a fresh session with handoff note

ucs.title: Archive completed work folder
ucs.summary: When the user confirms a work is done, devbench checks dirty/untracked/unpushed/ignored state, closes the 1:1 Herdr workspace and its recorded terminals first to release Windows file locks, detaches clean git worktrees while keeping branches, writes a frozen state snapshot + git summary, and moves the folder to the archive root.

flows.title: Herdr workspace closed, worktrees detached, and folder archived

touchpoints.sees: Confirmation showing closed Herdr workspace, preserved branch SHAs, frozen snapshot, and final archive path

flows.title: Dirty or untracked files found in a worktree

touchpoints.sees: Archive blocked before closing Herdr; affected paths listed with --snapshot-wip option (no silent force)

flows.title: Windows file lock or interrupted cross-drive move

touchpoints.sees: archive_phase checkpoint saved in central state; rerun resumes cleanly from the failed step

flows.title: Archive invoked from inside the work's own Herdr workspace

touchpoints.sees: State flushed safely and caller warned to close its own workspace last or run from Dispatcher

flows.title: Herdr space already closed or archive folder name collides

touchpoints.sees: Stale Herdr IDs tolerated, timestamp suffix appended on collision, unrelated spaces untouched

ucs.title: Keep main Git checkouts clean and conflict-free
ucs.summary: Existing local repositories continue working normally alongside devbench worktrees: branch-checkout collisions are prevented, ignored files are flagged before removal, and git worktree metadata is pruned cleanly after archiving.

flows.title: Source repo stays clean after worktree lifecycle

touchpoints.sees: git worktree list shows no stale entries and main checkout stays untouched

flows.title: Target branch already checked out in main repo

touchpoints.sees: Stops before mutating main checkout and prompts for a distinct task branch

flows.title: Gitignored files (e.g. .env) exist inside worktree

touchpoints.sees: Lists ignored files with soft warning before git worktree remove deletes the checkout

flows.title: Worktree directory was manually deleted outside devbench

touchpoints.sees: git worktree prune removes orphaned .git/worktrees metadata cleanly

ucs.title: Preserve user config across plugin updates
ucs.summary: Installing or updating devbench from its marketplace repo in Antigravity, Claude Code, or Codex leaves ~/.devbench/config.json untouched outside versioned plugin caches and reports any new template fields via config check.

flows.title: Plugin updates without clobbering external user config

touchpoints.sees: Existing ~/.devbench/config.json remains intact and passes schema check

flows.title: New version adds required template keys or bumps schema_version

touchpoints.sees: Lists missing keys with example snippet from config.example.json; never auto-overwrites user file

flows.title: Marketplace updater writes to a new versioned cache folder

touchpoints.sees: New cache directory reads the same external ~/.devbench/config.json seamlessly

flows.title: Contributor keeps a gitignored local config.json in repo clone

touchpoints.sees: External config wins when present; repo-local gitignored file used only in dev mode fallback

crud.delete: n/a: user removes external ~/.devbench/config.json manually on uninstall
n/a: archived intact rather than hard-deleted
n/a: retained in central state index with frozen snapshot copied into archive folder
